Drug Consequence: Effect on Nutrient Excretion
Since most drugs are excreted in urine, any drug that increases
urinary output places the patient at risk for accelerated nutrient 
excretion as well. A classic example is the use of diuretics that 
are potassium wasting. Use of the diuretic Lasix (furosemide)
or any other medications in this class can result in hypokalemia 
(low serum potassium). Any medication that aﬀ ects renal func-
tion in a signiﬁ cant way—reducing reabsorption of nutrients, 
for instance—can also cause excessive loss of a nutrient in the
